_what: Trail, highlight and route links per stop, with the evidence tier for each one.
_why: The trail boxes were built when direct listing URLs could not be found, so half the named trails render as a search magnifier (135 of 265 main-loop items, 129 of 233 extension items). They can be found now. This file is the source; build_links.py injects it into STOPS/EXT_DATA. Editing the consts by hand is silently overwritten by the next build.

_tiers.official: Fetched from the managing authority (state park, NPS, USFS) and confirmed 200 with the expected content type, from this machine.
_tiers.indexed: Returned by web search with a matching title and a review count. The page itself could NOT be loaded — alltrails.com answers 403 to every request from here, so a 403 proves nothing either way. Real, but one tier below official.
_tiers.unlisted: Confirmed to exist by the managing authority, but no AllTrails listing found. Deliberately carries no trail link rather than a search that goes nowhere.

_match.exact: The official trail and the AllTrails listing are the same object.
_match.contains: The AllTrails listing is a longer user-assembled route that includes this official trail. Both are shown; the official name and length stay primary.

_uses: From the managing authority, not inferred. hike | bike | horse.
_cruise: true only where reviews support riding it at cruising pace on gravel tyres: rail-grade or packed surface, no walk sections, no puncture-hazard reports. Bike-legal is not sufficient. Technical singletrack is bike-legal nearly everywhere and is not what this flags.
_dogs: Stop-level dog rule where the managing authority publishes one. This trip carries a dog for 405 nights; a stop where dogs are banned from every trail needs to say so on the card.

biking.name: Caprock Canyons Trailway
biking.official_length: 64 mi, former Fort Worth & Denver rail bed, through the 742-ft Clarity Tunnel
biking.cruise_reason: Ruled out on rider reports, not on paper. Surface is a sand-and-clay mix needing 700x35c minimum; rocky for the ~13 mi from South Plains to Clarity Tunnel; repeated goathead puncture reports; the tunnel itself is sandy and guano-covered and has to be walked. Described as remote and for prepared riders.
biking.reviews_note: No star rating surfaced for this listing in any search result — count only, not an omission in the data entry.

blurb_fix.problem: The activity card says the Trailway is 'a flat, packed-gravel former rail bed'. Riders describe sand and clay, rock, and goatheads. That description reads as an invitation to a casual ride.
blurb_fix.with: former rail bed — sand and clay, rocky in sections, gravel tyres and puncture kit

Bike or walk the Caprock Canyons Trailwa.cruise_reason: Sand and clay needing 700x35c, rocky for 13 mi, goathead punctures, and the tunnel has to be walked.

wind-river.problem: All three entries in the trail box were TRAILHEADS, not trails — car parks with signboards. Replaced with the actual routes that leave them, per the rule that a trail entry must be a trail and must carry distance, time, difficulty and reviews.
wind-river.seasonal: The stop's own blurb, note and red weather flag already say the alpine trailheads are snowed in at this date. The trail box was the only part of the card that did not. Arrival is 24 Apr 2027, seven nights. Every trail below is out of reach on this visit and is tagged as such rather than removed — the stop is a deliberate lower-elevation scouting stop and the real Wind River visit is Pinedale, late May 2028, on the East trip.

yosemite.dogs: PROHIBITED on trails "even if carried" — NPS states there are no exceptions for carried pets. Allowed on a few paved paths: Bridalveil Fall, Lower Yosemite Fall, the paved Cook's Meadow path, the paved road to Mirror Lake, Wawona Meadow Loop, and some Wawona/Hodgdon fire roads.

great-basin.dogs: PROHIBITED on most trails. Two exceptions: Lexington Arch Trail, and the trail between Baker and the Great Basin Visitor Center. Leash 6 ft.
great-basin.dogs_exception: Lexington Arch Trail and the Baker-to-visitor-centre trail only.

joshua-tree.dogs: PROHIBITED on hiking trails and in the backcountry. Two paved exceptions — Oasis of Mara and Keys View — plus anywhere a vehicle can go, within 100 ft of roads, parking or campgrounds.

death-valley.dogs: PROHIBITED on trails and in wilderness, "even when carried in backpacks, purses, or strollers". Leashed dogs are fine wherever a car can go — paved and unpaved roads, parking, campgrounds. Titus Canyon Road is a road, so it counts; Golden Canyon does not.

grand-teton.dogs: PROHIBITED. NPS: "Pets are prohibited on trails, pathways, beaches, in buildings, and swimming in any park waters." Also banned on the multi-use pathway and beyond 30 ft from roadways. Permitted in campgrounds, turnouts, picnic areas and on roads — and in the surrounding Bridger-Teton National Forest, which is the workaround here.

sequoia-kings-canyon.dogs: PROHIBITED on ALL trails, explicitly including the paved ones — NPS names the General Sherman Tree Trail, Big Trees Trail and Grant Tree Trail. Pets are allowed only in parking lots, on paved roads, in campgrounds and picnic areas. Every one of this stop's five trails is closed to the dog, including the Christmas ones.

bar-harbor-me.dogs: ALLOWED on most trails — 100 miles of trail and 45 miles of carriage road, leash 6 ft. Acadia is one of the most dog-friendly national parks on this entire trip. Six trails are closed to pets outright: Precipice, BEEHIVE, Ladder Trail to Dorr Mountain, Beech Cliffs, Perpendicular (Mansell Mountain), and Jordan Cliffs between Penobscot East Trail and the carriage road. Nine more are "not recommended".
bar-harbor-me.dogs_note: The Beehive is named on this card AND is one of the six trails Acadia closes to dogs — the iron-rung climb. Everything else here is open to the dog, including Cadillac South Ridge and Gorham Mountain.

staunton-va.dogs: ALLOWED on most trails — Shenandoah is one of the few national parks that permits dogs on trails, with fewer than 20 of 500+ trail miles off-limits. Leash 6 ft, physical leash. Prohibited: Fox Hollow, STONY MAN (blue-blazed portion to the summit), Limberlost, the Old Rag trails, Post Office Junction to Old Rag Shelter, Dark Hollow Falls, Story of the Forest, Bearfence Mountain and Frazier Discovery.
staunton-va.dogs_note: Two of this stop's trails are on Shenandoah's short prohibited list — Stony Man's blue-blazed summit portion and the Old Rag trails (Ridge Access, Ridge, Saddle). Everything ELSE in the park is open to the dog, which still makes this one of the best stops on the trip for walking together; it is just that both trails currently named here happen to be exceptions. Worth adding dog-legal Shenandoah trails to this card.

bryson-city-nc.dogs: PROHIBITED on trails, with exactly two exceptions: the Gatlinburg Trail and the Oconaluftee River Trail. Leash 6 ft on those. NPS actively discourages bringing pets because most trails are off-limits.
bryson-city-nc.dogs_exception: Gatlinburg Trail and Oconaluftee River Trail only.
bryson-city-nc.dogs_note: Oconaluftee is the accessible one from this side — the Bryson City stop already names the Oconaluftee Visitor Center in its highlights, so the dog-legal walk is the one you were going to anyway.

_dogs_verdict: Per stop: 'allowed' | 'prohibited' | 'partial' | absent. Absent means NOT RESEARCHED and renders no icon at all — a missing dog rule must never look like a green light. 'partial' means the authority names some trails and not others, so the verdict lives on the trail, not the stop.
_activities: Per-stop overrides for the highlights list. Each entry maps an activity's name to a verified entity: its real Wikipedia article, its direct AllTrails listing where it IS a trail, and the official page. Activities with an entry render real links and pills; activities without one keep the generic name-derived search links, which is the honest fallback until they are researched. `drop: true` removes a duplicate restatement of another activity.
_url_provenance: EVERY url here must be COPIED from a search result that returned it. Never construct a slug from a trail's name — alltrails slugs are unpredictable (--2, --3 suffixes, reworded titles) and a fabricated one looks exactly like a real one until it 404s in front of you at a trailhead. This rule exists because four urls were built from names in this file; three happened to be right and one was not, which is luck, not verification.
_auto: Entries marked auto:true were resolved by resolve_highlights.py — the headline reduced to candidate entity names and checked against Wikipedia's real article index. Exact hits only; a fuzzy match is treated as no match. Hand-written entries are richer and are never overwritten.
